entries.name: Build an AI API on Hosted Inference Providers
entries.description: Build and deploy an AI API on Railway that calls hosted inference providers for model output. Covers provider selection, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, streaming, timeouts, and provider fallback.

entries.name: Build an LLM Gateway in TypeScript
entries.description: Build and deploy an LLM gateway on Railway that issues its own API keys, enforces per-key token budgets, and tracks spend across teams. One place to hold provider keys instead of scattering them across services.

entries.name: Build and Deploy Your Own MCP Server
entries.description: Build a remote MCP server in TypeScript with Streamable HTTP transport and deploy it on Railway. Expose your app's data as tools that AI assistants like Claude and Cursor can call over the network.

entries.name: Choose Between Local and Remote MCP Servers
entries.description: When an MCP server should run locally over stdio and when it should be a remote Streamable HTTP service. Decision factors, what the 2026 spec changed, and how to deploy the remote kind on Railway.

entries.name: Connect the Best MCP Servers to Your Coding Agent
entries.description: Config snippets for connecting nine widely used MCP servers to Claude Code, Cursor, and VS Code, covering GitHub, Postgres, browser automation, docs lookup, error tracking, and deployment.

entries.name: Deploy a Claude Agent SDK App
entries.description: Deploy a Claude Agent SDK service on Railway that runs agent tasks over HTTP, streams progress as NDJSON, and stays inside the platform's request limits.

entries.name: Deploy a LangGraph Agent Backend
entries.description: Run a LangGraph agent as a FastAPI service on Railway with Postgres checkpointing for durable conversation state and Claude as the LLM.

entries.name: Deploy a Multi-Agent System on Railway
entries.description: Deploy multiple AI agents as separate Railway services that communicate via Redis and Postgres. Includes working orchestrator and agent code, inter-service communication, and independent scaling.

entries.name: Deploy a RAG Pipeline with pgvector
entries.description: Build a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline on Railway using Postgres with pgvector for vector storage, an external embedding API, and an LLM for generation. Covers document ingestion, similarity search, and deployment.

entries.name: Deploy a Vibe-Coded App on Railway
entries.description: Deploy an application built with AI coding tools like Cursor, Claude Code, Bolt, or Lovable on Railway. Covers common deployment issues with AI-generated code and how to fix them.

entries.name: Deploy an AI Agent with Async Workers
entries.description: Run AI agent workflows on Railway with an API service, async workers via Redis queue, and Postgres for state persistence. Covers CPU-based agent patterns without GPU.

entries.name: Deploy an AI Chatbot with Streaming Responses
entries.description: Deploy a chatbot on Railway that streams LLM responses token by token using Server-Sent Events. Covers Next.js with the AI SDK, API key management, and optional conversation persistence with Postgres.

entries.name: Deploy an AI-Powered Bot for Discord or Telegram
entries.description: Deploy a Discord or Telegram bot on Railway that uses LLM APIs for conversational responses. Covers always-on deployment, API key management, conversation memory with Postgres, and rate limit handling.

entries.name: Deploy an AI-Powered SaaS App on Railway
entries.description: Deploy a production AI-powered SaaS application on Railway with an Express backend, Postgres database, and external LLM API integration. Covers API key management, request caching, rate limiting, and async processing for longer tasks.

entries.name: Deploy an LLM Gateway with LiteLLM
entries.description: Deploy LiteLLM Proxy on Railway as an LLM gateway for multiple providers. Covers model routing, cost tracking, API key management, caching with Redis, and private networking.

entries.name: Estimate the Cost of Running AI Agents
entries.description: What an always-on AI agent costs to run. How to calculate LLM API spend per run, what the hosting compute actually costs on Railway's usage-based pricing, and where the money goes as you scale.

entries.name: Run an Embeddings Pipeline with an External API and pgvector
entries.description: Deploy a batch worker on Railway that generates embeddings through an external API and stores them in Postgres with pgvector. Covers schema design, safe concurrent processing, and the psycopg2 vector adaptation gotcha.

entries.name: Run Code-Execution Sandboxes for AI Agents
entries.description: Run AI-generated code in isolated, disposable sandboxes on Railway. What a code-execution sandbox is, why agents need one, and how to create, checkpoint, fork, and destroy sandboxes from the CLI or the TypeScript SDK.

entries.name: Running Agents on Railway
entries.description: Learn how to deploy always-on, autonomous AI agents on Railway by building a Claude-powered GitHub DevBot that opens pull requests in response to new issues.

entries.name: Self-Host Dify
entries.description: Deploy Dify on Railway with Postgres, Redis, and persistent storage. Build AI applications, RAG pipelines, and agent workflows through Dify's visual interface.

entries.name: Self-Host Flowise
entries.description: Deploy Flowise on Railway with persistent storage and authentication. Build LLM chains, agents, and chatbots through a visual drag-and-drop interface without managing servers.

entries.name: Self-Host Open WebUI
entries.description: Deploy Open WebUI on Railway to get a ChatGPT-like interface that connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, and other LLM providers. Includes persistent storage and authentication setup.

entries.name: Use Agents in Railway Sandboxes
entries.description: Drive Railway sandboxes from your local AI coding agent. Spin up isolated environments for development, run agents against your real infrastructure, and use the create, configure, checkpoint, and fork loop to move fast.

entries.name: Use Object Storage for AI Agent Outputs
entries.description: Store AI agent artifacts in S3-compatible object storage on Railway. Where generated files, transcripts, and reports should live, how to write them from a worker, and how to share them with presigned URLs.

entries.name: Add Authentication to a Frontend Application
entries.description: Implement authentication in a frontend application deployed on Railway. Covers third-party providers (Clerk, Supabase Auth), session-based auth with Postgres, and common deployment pitfalls.

entries.name: Build Hybrid Search with Postgres Full-Text Search and pgvector
entries.description: Combine Postgres full-text search and pgvector similarity search in one database, then merge results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Includes schema, SQL, and a deployable Node API.

entries.name: Choose Between Cron Jobs, Background Workers, and Queues
entries.description: When to use cron jobs, always-on workers, and message queues for background processing. Covers tradeoffs, failure modes, and how to run each pattern on Railway.

entries.name: Choose Between SSE and WebSockets
entries.description: When to use Server-Sent Events vs WebSockets for real-time data. Covers protocol differences, reconnection handling, and how to deploy both on Railway.

entries.name: Choose Between SSR, SSG, and ISR for Your Frontend
entries.description: When to use server-side rendering, static site generation, or incremental static regeneration. Covers Railway deployment implications, cost tradeoffs, and framework support.

entries.name: Configure Client-Side Routing for Single-Page Applications
entries.description: Set up Caddy or Nginx to handle client-side routing for single-page applications on Railway. Avoid blank pages on refresh and configure fallback routes.

entries.name: Deploy a Full-Stack Next.js App with Postgres, Background Jobs, and File Uploads
entries.description: Deploy a production Next.js application on Railway with a Postgres database, Redis-backed background workers, and file uploads via storage buckets. Covers multi-service architecture and production hardening.

entries.name: Deploy a SaaS Backend with Postgres, Workers, and Webhooks
entries.description: Set up a production SaaS backend on Railway with an API service, Postgres database, background worker, and cron job for webhook processing.

entries.name: GitHub Actions Post-Deploy
entries.description: Learn how to use GitHub Actions to run post-deployment commands.

entries.name: GitHub Actions PR Environment
entries.description: Learn how to use the CLI in a GitHub Action to create environments for PRs

entries.name: GitHub Actions Self Hosted Runners
entries.description: Learn how to deploy your own scalable self hosted GitHub Actions Runners on Railway. Build your own fleet of runners for your Enterprise and then scale your self-hosted runners with Railway replicas for blazing fast builds.

entries.name: Isolate Staging from Production for Compliance
entries.description: Separate staging and production on Railway with per-environment networks, per-environment bucket instances, and environment-scoped credentials.

entries.name: Manage Environment Variables in Frontend Builds
entries.description: Understand build-time vs runtime environment variables in frontend frameworks. Covers Vite, Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Astro, and Angular prefix conventions and how Railway handles each.

entries.name: Receive Webhooks at Scale
entries.description: Build a webhook receiver that verifies signatures, responds fast, and queues work for a background worker. Covers idempotency keys, retries, and how to run the pattern on Railway.

entries.name: Run Redis as a Cache vs a Persistent Store
entries.description: Configure Redis as a cache or as a durable store on Railway. Covers the persistence settings, eviction policies, and start commands for each mode.

entries.name: Schedule, Retry, and Dead-Letter Jobs with BullMQ
entries.description: Run BullMQ on Railway with a Redis service and an always-on worker. Covers repeatable job schedules, retries with exponential backoff, and a dead-letter queue pattern.

entries.name: Serve a Multi-Region API with Failover
entries.description: Run one API service across multiple Railway regions with replicas, nearest-region routing, and automatic replica restarts. Covers routing behavior, health checks, and what failover Railway gives you.

entries.name: Stream AI Responses to a Frontend with Server-Sent Events
entries.description: Stream LLM tokens from an API service to a frontend using Server-Sent Events on Railway. Covers Express and Hono server implementations, client-side consumption, and reconnection handling.

entries.name: Use Storage Buckets for Uploads, Exports, and Assets
entries.description: Set up Railway storage buckets for file uploads via presigned URLs, background export generation, and asset serving through a backend proxy.

entries.name: Host a Documentation Site with Astro Starlight
entries.description: Build a documentation site with Astro Starlight and deploy it to Railway, with full-text search, a structured sidebar, and a custom domain.

entries.name: Add Connection Pooling to Postgres with PgBouncer
entries.description: Why Postgres needs a connection pooler, how to add PgBouncer to a Railway Postgres service, and how to configure your application for pooled and unpooled connections.

entries.name: Autoscale a Service Horizontally Based on Load
entries.description: Build an autoscaler on Railway that measures load in your application and adjusts replica counts through the Public API, the CLI, or a cron schedule.

entries.name: Back Up and Restore Postgres
entries.description: Set up volume backups and point-in-time recovery for Postgres on Railway, take logical dumps with pg_dump, and run a restore drill so you know recovery works before you need it.

entries.name: Cut Idle Costs with Serverless Mode
entries.description: Enable Serverless on Railway to sleep idle services and stop paying for compute they do not use. Covers the outbound-traffic sleep trigger and the cold boot tradeoff.

entries.name: Debug a Production Incident with Logs, Metrics, and Traces
entries.description: A step-by-step incident debugging workflow using Railway's built-in observability surfaces. Confirm scope with metrics, find the failure in HTTP and deployment logs, correlate requests, and mitigate with a rollback.

entries.name: Deploy an OpenTelemetry Collector and Backend on Railway
entries.description: Monitor and trace your applications by deploying an OpenTelemetry Collector and backend on Railway.

entries.name: Deploy from a Private Container Registry
entries.description: Deploy Docker images from private registries (GHCR, Docker Hub, GitLab, ECR, Google Artifact Registry) on Railway, from credential setup to CI-driven redeploys.

entries.name: Deploy Node.js & Express API with Autoscaling, Secrets, and Zero Downtime
entries.description: Learn how to deploy Node.js and Express applications with automatic scaling, environment secrets, zero-downtime updates, and preview environments, all without managing servers or learning Kubernetes/container orchestration.

entries.name: Deploy on Merge with PR Environments as Canaries
entries.description: Set up a trunk-based promotion workflow on Railway. Every pull request gets a canary environment; every merge to main deploys production automatically.

entries.name: Deploy Static Sites with Zero Configuration and Custom Domains
entries.description: Learn how to deploy static websites to Railway with automatic GitHub builds, SSL certificates, custom domains, and integrate with a CDN. Perfect for marketing sites, blogs, and documentation.

entries.name: Deploying a Monorepo to Railway
entries.description: Learn how to deploy a monorepo to Railway.

entries.name: Handle Build-Time vs Runtime Secrets in Docker Builds
entries.description: When Docker builds on Railway can see your variables, how to pass build secrets with ARG, and why runtime secrets should never be baked into the image.

entries.name: Instrument an App with OpenTelemetry
entries.description: Add OpenTelemetry traces and metrics to a Node.js or Python app on Railway, and send them to a collector over the private network.

entries.name: Load Test an App Before Launch with k6
entries.description: Write a k6 load test, run it locally or as a Railway service, set realistic performance targets, and read Railway metrics while the test runs.

entries.name: Lock Down a Production Railway Project
entries.description: Harden a production Railway project with Under Attack Mode, private networking, scoped API tokens, sealed variables, and workspace-level access controls.

entries.name: Managing Secrets on Railway
entries.description: How to store API keys, database URLs, and other secrets on Railway using service, shared, reference, and sealed variables, with no separate secrets manager.

entries.name: Migrate a Production Database into Railway with Minimal Downtime
entries.description: Move a production PostgreSQL database into Railway using dump and restore or logical replication, with a cutover checklist that keeps downtime to seconds.

entries.name: Preview Deployments with PR Environments
entries.description: Learn how to use Railway PR Environments to spin up isolated, ephemeral preview deployments for every pull request, including Focused and Bot PR Environments.

entries.name: Right-Size CPU and Memory from Real Metrics
entries.description: How to read the Metrics tab on Railway, translate real CPU and memory usage into a monthly cost, and set replica and usage limits that cap spend without crashing your service.

entries.name: Roll Back a Bad Deploy Fast
entries.description: How to revert a broken deployment on Railway in under a minute. Covers rollback vs redeploy vs restart, image retention limits, and healthcheck-gated deploys that stop bad code before it goes live.

entries.name: Rotate API Keys and Database Credentials Without Downtime
entries.description: Use the dual-key overlap pattern, staged redeploys, and reference variables to rotate secrets on Railway with zero downtime.

entries.name: Scaling Your Application
entries.description: Learn how to scale applications on Railway with vertical autoscaling and horizontal replicas, and how to read metrics to right-size each service.

entries.name: Set Up Alerts for Crashes, Restarts, and Failed Deploys
entries.description: Configure Railway webhooks and monitors to get notified in Slack, Discord, or your own service when a deployment fails, crashes, or a resource threshold is crossed.

entries.name: Set Up Structured Logging for a Production App
entries.description: Emit JSON logs from your Railway services so the Log Explorer can parse, color, and filter them by level and custom attributes.

entries.name: Speed Up a Global App with Cache-Control Headers and a CDN
entries.description: Set Cache-Control headers correctly for static assets, HTML, and API responses, then put a CDN in front of your Railway service to serve users from the nearest edge.

entries.name: Add a CDN using Amazon CloudFront
entries.description: Learn how to integrate Amazon CloudFront as a CDN for your Fastify app in this step-by-step guide.

entries.name: Connect a Third-Party Observability Tool
entries.description: Send telemetry from your Railway services to third-party observability tools. Covers vendor SDKs (Datadog, New Relic, Sentry), OpenTelemetry (OTLP), and common deployment pitfalls.

entries.name: Create a Bridge from Railway to AWS RDS with Tailscale
entries.description: Learn how to securely access your AWS RDS database from Railway using a Tailscale subnet router.

entries.name: Deploy a Docker Compose App to Production
entries.description: Map a Docker Compose configuration to Railway services. Covers service mapping, networking, volumes, environment variables, and databases.

entries.name: Deploy a Jupyter Server for Team Data Work
entries.description: Run a shared JupyterLab server on Railway with token authentication, a persistent volume for notebooks, and health checks for zero-downtime deploys.

entries.name: Deploy a Lovable App on Railway
entries.description: Learn how to deploy applications generated by Lovable.dev to Railway. This guide covers the workflow from prompt-based generation to continuous deployment.

entries.name: Deploy a WebSocket Application with Socket.IO
entries.description: Deploy a Socket.IO server and client on Railway. Covers CORS configuration, reconnection handling, and scaling with a Redis adapter.

entries.name: Deploy Caddy
entries.description: Learn how to deploy Caddy on Railway with one-click templates or CLI. This guide covers how to choose plugins, and configure static sites and reverse proxies.

entries.name: Deploy RabbitMQ and Wire Up Producers and Consumers
entries.description: Run RabbitMQ on Railway, expose the management UI, and connect producer and consumer services over private networking with Node.js and amqplib.

entries.name: Run ClickHouse for Product Analytics
entries.description: Deploy ClickHouse on Railway from the template or the official Docker image, size its volume for event data, and ingest and query analytics events from a Node.js service.

entries.name: Run Playwright in a Docker Container
entries.description: Deploy Playwright scripts on Railway using a Docker container with browser dependencies, font packages, and memory configuration.

entries.name: Self-host Ghost with MySQL and Custom Themes
entries.description: Deploy Ghost on Railway from the official Docker image with a MySQL database, persistent content storage, and custom domain configuration.

entries.name: Self-Host Keycloak for Authentication
entries.description: Deploy Keycloak on Railway with a Postgres database, an admin account, and a public domain. Configure a realm and an OIDC client for your applications.

entries.name: Self-Host Langfuse for LLM Observability
entries.description: Deploy Langfuse v3 on Railway with Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis, and object storage. Trace, debug, and evaluate your LLM applications on infrastructure you control.

entries.name: Self-host n8n
entries.description: Deploy n8n on Railway with persistent storage and webhook configuration. Run your own workflow automation instance without managing servers.

entries.name: Self-host Payload CMS with Postgres
entries.description: Deploy Payload CMS 3.x on Railway inside a Next.js application. Covers database setup, media storage with buckets, and production configuration.

entries.name: Self-host Strapi with Postgres and File Uploads
entries.description: Deploy Strapi on Railway with a Postgres database and persistent file storage. Covers one-click template deployment, environment configuration, and upload provider setup.

entries.name: Self-host Supabase with Postgres, Auth, and Storage
entries.description: Deploy the Supabase stack on Railway with Postgres, GoTrue auth, PostgREST API, storage, and the Studio dashboard. Covers multi-service setup and JWT configuration.

entries.name: Self-Host Uptime Kuma for Uptime Monitoring
entries.description: Deploy Uptime Kuma on Railway with a volume for persistent monitor history. Monitor public sites and internal services, and publish status pages.

entries.name: Set Up a Datadog Agent in Railway
entries.description: Learn how to set up a Datadog agent in Railway.

entries.name: Set up a Tailscale Forwarder
entries.description: Learn how to access services on your private network on Railway by using a Tailscale Forwarder.

entries.name: Ship Application Logs to a Third-Party Aggregator
entries.description: Build a log drain on Railway with a Vector forwarder service. Apps send logs over private networking, and Vector fans them out to any aggregator.

entries.name: Sync Secrets from an External Secrets Manager
entries.description: Keep Doppler, Infisical, or Vault as your source of truth and push secrets into Railway variables with the Public API, a sync script, or a vendor integration.
